author: Peach Tree Times
title: Veterans honored at Normandy as Delta concludes commemorative program
text:
Veterans participated in a flag-raising ceremony at the Normandy American Cemetery on June 10, marking the final full day of their visit before the grounds opened to the public. Fred Nungesser, Keith Lancaster, Hibby Margol, and Calvin Shiner assisted in raising the flag during a quiet moment.
Afterward, the group traveled to Omaha Beach for lunch. Ed Sandy walked onto the sand for the first time since D-Day 82 years ago. On June 6, 1944, Sandy served as a gunner aboard LCF-3, a Landing Craft Flak positioned offshore that provided anti-aircraft support to incoming forces. In subsequent weeks, his vessel was involved in rescue and transport operations along Normandy’s coast.
Upon returning to their hotel, Delta Airport Customer Service team members from Paris and Madrid created an airport-style check-in area with bag drop and boarding pass printing ahead of a special charter flight departing from Deauville. The following morning included breakfast with students and team members from Delta Air Lines, Best Defense Foundation, and Michelin. Veterans signed booklets and keepsakes before boarding their flight while French schoolchildren sang “Amazing Grace” and “We’ll Meet Again” by Vera Lynn.
Delta Air Lines will continue its efforts to connect veterans with future generations through programs such as the WWII Ambassador Program in partnership with GrandPad tablet company. Upon arrival back in the United States, more than 50 Delta employees from various departments volunteered their time assisting veterans during connections to their final destinations.
Delta Air Lines utilizes a fleet comprising various aircraft models from manufacturers such as Airbus and Boeing; connects more than 350 destinations across multiple continents; operates scheduled passenger and cargo transport worldwide; functions as a leading global carrier; focuses on linking people globally through secure air travel; and is incorporated in Delaware under U.S. law, according to the official website.
